title: Row–column symmetry and contraction of coordinate sweeps
main_claim: Theorem 1.1: there are weights D^{3/4} <= W_λ <= D_λ and bounded exponents p_d <= p_* with W_λ ||K_d(λ)||_{p_d}^{p_d} <= 1 for all λ ⊢ 2^d. So ||K_d(λ)||_op <= D_λ^{-3/(4p_*)}. Corollary 1.2: the full-deck Thorp shuffle mixes in t_mix(d) = Θ(d) physical shuffles, with lower bound ⌈(2/N)log2(3N!/4)⌉ = 2d−O(1).

issues.location: weighted.tex, Sec. 'A sparse forest estimate', eq. (ten:weighted:eq:1)
issues.description: The row-sum bound for K*D is only sketched: the pre-sampling of path types independent of S, forest-shape counting C_0^k, and the (2d)^{k-c} embedding count are asserted with little detail. I checked the structure and it appears correct: the inclusion–exclusion gives a no-isolated-vertex condition, column sums are <= 2^k, the negative-dependence bound Pr(S ⊇ F) <= (k/N)^{|F|} is preserved by switches, binom(N,c) <= (CN/k)^{k/2}, and the Schur test gives the k/8 exponent. Still, a referee would ask for more detail here.
issues.evidence: 'We may pre-sample, independently of S, two options at every starting position...'; 'the expected number of embeddings ... is at most (2d)^{k-c}'
